 Volodymyr Zelensky, centre, with Jared Kushner, left, and Steve Witkoff after their meeting at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, west of Dublin
 Credit : AFP via Getty Images/PAUL FAITH
 Joe Barnes
 Diplomatic Editor. 
 James Crisp
 Europe Editor
 Published 
 13 November 2026 11:33am GMT
 Vladimir Putin is “willing to give it a try” with European negotiators to find peace in Ukraine , Jared Kushner has claimed.
 Donald Trump’s peace envoy, also his son-in-law, said the Russian president had agreed to include Europe in peace negotiations after late-night talks on an airfield outside Dublin with Volodymyr Zelensky.
 Mr Kushner and Steve Witkoff, his negotiating partner , met the Ukrainian president during a refuelling stop while travelling from Moscow to the US.
 However, Moscow said it had not yet agreed to entering into talks with Europe.
 Dmitry Peskov, a Kremlin spokesman, said on Friday: “Once we understand their real intentions and their willingness to contribute to the peace process, then we can make a decision on holding talks in an expanded format.
 “If the Europeans really do have someone who is at least authorised in some way to talk, and if the Europeans really do have the desire to do so, then of course we will be ready to talk to them.”
 Vladimir Putin met Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in Moscow on Thursday
 Credit : AFP/Vyacheslav Prokofyev
 Mr Kushner’s and Mr Peskov’s comments will act as a starter pistol on a separate effort by divided European governments to find a single representative to speak on their behalf.
 “We cannot conclude this deal without the Europeans being at the table,” said Mr Kushner.
 The American negotiators also met officials from the UK, EU, France, Germany, Poland and Nato, who until now have led Europe’s representation.
 EU leaders will discuss potential candidates when they meet for talks in the Irish capital on Friday. 
 Countries are deeply divided over how to respond to Putin accepting that Europe should be allowed to join the talks. Some, mainly eastern Europeans, believe it is a trap designed for them to redraw the continent’s security architecture as the price for peace.
 Others believe discussions with the Russians are a necessary step to ending the long-running war.
 Mr Zelensky told European leaders in Dublin: “Europe really needs to pay attention.”
 The Ukrainian president warned them that US-Russian talks risked encroaching on Europe’s sovereignty, especially on security guarantees.
 “When the Americans and Russians talk about these, it’s not just about Ukraine – in fact, it’s more about some kind of new security framework between Europe and Russia. And we find this approach a bit strange,” he said.
 Latvia’s prime minister said Europe had to be braver in facing down Russia as he arrived for the EU summit on Friday.
 “I think we as Europe have to grow some bigger balls. We are bigger in military might, in all the economic aspects,” he said.
 It was not up to “the aggressor, which is losing on the front line” to decide Europe’s security architecture, he added.
 Micheál Martin, the Irish prime minister, said he hoped “today’s discussions will bring clarity” over who will represent Europe in the talks on Friday morning. He said he expected the issue to be settled within the next fortnight.
 David Blair
 Putin's plan for Europe is already written in black and white
 Read more 
 After the European Political Community summit on Thursday, Antonio Costa, the European Council president, said: “Europe has consigned empires and zones of influence to the dustbin of history. We will never allow for them to come to life again.
 “The future of European security cannot be discussed and decided without Europe.”
 Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said it was for EU leaders to identify their own representatives for any future talks with Russia.
 “All the leaders I’ve spoken to today are determined to put a bit of a ring of steel around Zelensky as part of all of this to back him up to the hilt, and that’s what we will do,” Mr Burnham told reporters on Thursday.
 He said European security would not be up for negotiation with Putin in any future talks, adding: “The very clear feeling here today, as well as wanting to see progress towards a ceasefire and doing everything we can to achieve that. But we don’t want to see escalation. We want to see the opposite.”
